ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a small block placed on a gray inclined plane, and the slope angle α is marked between the plane and the horizontal reference direction; the coefficient of friction μ is marked on the plane; in the coordinate axes, z is vertically upward, and x is along the downhill horizontal projection direction in the figure. The problem statement says that the magnetic field B0 is perpendicular to the inclined plane, so when the charged block moves within the inclined plane, the Lorentz force lies within the inclined plane and is perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity. Reasoning: After a very long time, take the terminal state, and the resultant force within the inclined plane is zero. The magnitude of the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sin α. The magnitude of the friction force is μN = μmg cos α, and its direction is opposite to the velocity. The magnetic field is perpendicular to the inclined plane, so the magnitude of the Lorentz force is QB0v, and it is within the inclined plane and perpendicular to the velocity. Decompose the component of gravity along the inclined plane into the velocity direction and the direction parallel to the magnetic force: the component along the velocity direction balances the friction force, that is, the corresponding magnitude is μmg cos α; the remaining component perpendicular to the velocity direction is balanced by the magnetic force. Therefore QB0v = sqrt[(mg sin α)^2 - (μmg cos α)^2]. Comparing with v = β mg/(QB0), obtain β = sqrt(sin^2 α - μ^2 cos^2 α). Substitute α = 40°, μ = 0.3: β = sqrt(sin^2 40° - 0.3^2 cos^2 40°) ≈ sqrt(0.4132 - 0.0528) ≈ sqrt(0.3604) ≈ 0.600.

raw_record.question_text: A small block of mass $m$ and charge $Q$ is placed at rest on an inclined plane with a slope $\alpha=40^{\circ}$. The coefficient of friction between them is $\mu=0.3$. A homogeneous magnetic field of magnitude $B_{0}$ is applied perpendicular to the slope. The speed of the block after a very long time is given by $v=\beta \frac{mg}{Q B_{0}}$. Determine $\beta$. Do not neglect the effects of gravity.

method.method_draft: Use a terminal-force triangle in the plane. Read from the image that the block moves on an inclined plane and that the slope angle alpha is measured between the plane and the horizontal downhill direction; the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane, so the Lorentz force lies within the plane and is perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity. From the text, take alpha=40 degrees, mu=0.3, field magnitude B0, and terminal speed form v=beta mg/(QB0). At very long time set the in-plane net force to zero. The downhill gravity component has magnitude mg sin alpha. Kinetic friction has magnitude mu mg cos alpha opposite the velocity. Magnetic force has magnitude QB0 v perpendicular to the velocity. Resolve the gravity component into parts parallel and perpendicular to the velocity: the parallel part balances friction, and the perpendicular part balances magnetic force. Thus QB0 v = sqrt[(mg sin alpha)^2 - (mu mg cos alpha)^2], so beta = sqrt(sin^2 alpha - mu^2 cos^2 alpha). Substituting alpha=40 degrees and mu=0.3 gives beta approximately 0.6.

图像描述：图中有一个小块放在灰色倾斜平面上，平面与水平参考方向之间标出坡角 α；平面上标有摩擦系数 μ；坐标轴中 z 竖直向上，x 沿图中下坡水平投影方向。题干说明磁场 B0 垂直于斜面，因此带电块在斜面内运动时，洛伦兹力位于斜面内并垂直于瞬时速度。

推理：很长时间后取终端状态，斜面内合力为零。重力沿斜面向下的分量大小为 mg sin α。摩擦力大小为 μN = μmg cos α，方向与速度相反。磁场垂直斜面，所以洛伦兹力大小为 QB0v，且在斜面内垂直于速度。将重力沿斜面的分量分解到速度方向和平行于磁力方向：沿速度方向的分量平衡摩擦力，即对应大小为 μmg cos α；垂直速度方向的剩余分量由磁力平衡。因此 QB0v = sqrt[(mg sin α)^2 - (μmg cos α)^2]。与 v = β mg/(QB0) 比较，得到 β = sqrt(sin^2 α - μ^2 cos^2 α)。代入 α = 40°，μ = 0.3：β = sqrt(sin^2 40° - 0.3^2 cos^2 40°) ≈ sqrt(0.4132 - 0.0528) ≈ sqrt(0.3604) ≈ 0.600。

method.method_draft: Write explicit steady-state component equations in axes attached to the plane. Read from the image an x-axis along the downhill slope and a y-axis across the plane; take the magnetic field along the plane normal. From the text use alpha=40 degrees, mu=0.3, and B=B0. Let the terminal velocity be v_x xhat + v_y yhat with speed v. ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A small block of mass $m$ and charge $Q$ is placed at rest on an inclined plane with a slope $\alpha=40^{\circ}$. The coefficient of friction between them is $\mu=0.3$. A homogeneous magnetic field of magnitude $B_{0}$ is applied perpendicular to the slope. The speed of the block after a very long time is given by $v=\beta \frac{mg}{Q B_{0}}$. Determine $\beta$. Do not neglect the effects of gravity.

The coefficient of friction between them is $\mu=0.3$. A homogeneous magnetic field of magnitude $B_{0}$ is applied perpendicular to the slope. The speed of the block after a very long time is given by $v=\beta \frac{mg}{Q B_{0}}$. Determine $\beta$. Do not neglect the effects of gravity.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, there is a small block placed on a gray inclined plane, and the slope angle α is marked between the plane and the horizontal reference direction; the coefficient of friction μ is marked on the plane; in the coordinate axes, z is vertically upward, and x is along the downhill horizontal projection direction in the figure. The problem statement says that the magnetic field B0 is perpendicular to the inclined plane, so when the charged block moves within the inclined plane, the Lorentz force lies within the inclined plane and is perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity.

Reasoning: After a very long time, take the terminal state, and the resultant force within the inclined plane is zero. The magnitude of the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sin α. The magnitude of the friction force is μN = μmg cos α, and its direction is opposite to the velocity. The magnetic field is perpendicular to the inclined plane, so the magnitude of the Lorentz force is QB0v, and it is within the inclined plane and perpendicular to the velocity. Decompose the component of gravity along the inclined plane into the velocity direction and the direction parallel to the magnetic force: the component along the velocity direction balances the friction force, that is, the corresponding magnitude is μmg cos α; the remaining component perpendicular to the velocity direction is balanced by the magnetic force. Therefore QB0v = sqrt[(mg sin α)^2 - (μmg cos α)^2]. Comparing with v = β mg/(QB0), obtain β = sqrt(sin^2 α - μ^2 cos^2 α). Substitute α = 40°, μ = 0.3: β = sqrt(sin^2 40° - 0.3^2 cos^2 40°) ≈ sqrt(0.4132 - 0.0528) ≈ sqrt(0.3604) ≈ 0.600.
